title: The best Skilario alternatives in 2026
lede: People look past Skilario for one of three reasons: the price, the refund terms, or wanting practice rather than reading. Here are the alternatives that answer each one, and one that doesn't.
keyTakeaways: Iro AI is the closest like-for-like alternative: short daily AI lessons, built on practice with feedback, at about half Skilario's App Store monthly price.
Khan Academy is the free option. Brilliant, DataCamp and Coursera suit foundations, data skills and certificates.
Coursiv teaches similar topics but sells the same way, through a web funnel with an intro price, so it does not fix a billing concern.
Whatever you pick, find the renewal price and the refund policy before you enter a card.
description: Looking for a Skilario alternative? Compare Iro AI, Coursiv, Brilliant, Khan Academy, DataCamp and Coursera by how they teach, what is free and how you pay.

sections.heading: The best Skilario alternatives
sections.html: The best Skilario alternative depends on why you are leaving. If you want to keep the daily-lesson format but actually practice with feedback, at a lower price and with Apple handling the billing, Iro AI is the closest fit. If you want it free, Khan Academy. For math and computer-science foundations, Brilliant; for data skills, DataCamp; for a formal certificate, Coursera. Most have a free tier, so you can try before paying.

sections.heading: Why people look for a Skilario alternative
sections.html:
Skilario is a new app that teaches ChatGPT, Claude and other AI tools in daily lessons of about ten minutes. The reasons people look elsewhere usually come down to three things:

  • Price. On the App Store it is $19.99 a month or $79.99 a year, and website plans can open with a promotional first payment that renews at the regular rate.
  • Refund terms. Skilario's terms rule out refunds for a change of mind, an unused subscription or dissatisfaction, and consider one only for a confirmed technical fault.
  • Method. Copying good prompts is a start. Writing your own and getting feedback on them is what builds the skill.

For the details, see our Skilario review, and if you are already subscribed, how to cancel Skilario first.

sections.heading: Why Iro AI is the closest alternative
sections.html:
Iro AI is our app, so read this as an interested party. If what drew you to Skilario was learning to use AI in a few minutes a day, Iro does the same job with a different method: practice instead of reading. You write real prompts in a Prompt Lab and get them scored, spot AI mistakes, and duel a skill-matched opponent, across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, prompting and more. It is often called the Duolingo for AI.

On the three reasons above:

  • Price. Free to start, with a battery that gives you a full lesson every day. Pro is $9.99 a month or $49.99 a year, with a 7-day free trial on the annual plan: about half Skilario's App Store monthly price, and $30 a year less.
  • Billing. Pro is billed by Apple, so cancelling is two taps in Settings and refunds go through Apple. No intro rate that converts to a higher one.
  • Method. 34 paths, 522 lessons and 3,000+ exercises across 23 exercise types, plus Ask Iro by chat and voice, an Image Lab, timed duels, Custom Paths built from a topic, link, screenshot or PDF, and certificates earned free and claimed with Pro.

sections.heading: A note on Coursiv
sections.html: Coursiv comes up in every search for apps like Skilario, and it covers similar ground. It also sells the same way: a web funnel with an intro offer that renews at a higher recurring price, and a money-back guarantee that pays out only if you used the app enough. If billing is why you are leaving Skilario, Coursiv does not fix it. The details are in how to cancel Coursiv, and there is a head-to-head in Iro AI vs Coursiv.

sections.heading: How to choose
sections.html:
• You learn by doing and want a daily habit → Iro AI.
  • You want it free → Khan Academy, or the Iro free tier.
  • You want math or CS theory → Brilliant.
  • You want data or coding skills → DataCamp.
  • You want a formal certificate → Coursera.

Before you subscribe to any of them, take a minute on the checkout page: find the renewal price, the renewal date and the refund policy. Our guide to spotting an AI subscription trap shows what to look for. Or see where your AI skills stand first with the free AI rank quiz, ten questions and about two minutes.

faq.q: What is the best Skilario alternative?
faq.a: It depends why you are leaving. Iro AI is the closest like-for-like alternative: short daily AI lessons built on practice with feedback, free to start, and about half Skilario's App Store monthly price. Khan Academy is free, Brilliant suits foundations, DataCamp data skills, and Coursera formal certificates.

faq.q: Is there a free alternative to Skilario?
faq.a: Yes. Khan Academy is free, and Iro AI is free to start with a full lesson every day. Brilliant, DataCamp and Coursera offer limited free access with paid upgrades.

faq.q: Is Iro AI cheaper than Skilario?
faq.a: On the App Store, yes. Iro Pro is $9.99 a month or $49.99 a year, with a 7-day free trial on the annual plan. Skilario lists $19.99 a month or $79.99 a year. Iro also has a free tier with a full lesson every day.

faq.q: Is Coursiv a good alternative to Skilario?
faq.a: It covers similar ground, but it sells the same way: a web funnel with an intro offer that renews at a higher recurring price, and a money-back guarantee that depends on how much you used the app. If billing is why you are leaving Skilario, Coursiv does not fix that.
